name: Cynthia Leis
summary: AEDG President/CEO AND PAAC Executive Director — the single locus of control over the economic-development trade-secret shield and the records custody for Project BOSC.
body:
## How she appears in the record

Cynthia "Cindy" Leis occupies **two seats at once** in the Project BOSC corpus:

- **President/CEO of the Allen Economic Development Group (AEDG)** — she signs the
  Elida Local School District notice letters as AEDG President/CEO (`leisc@aedg.org`),
  and the PAAC board minutes track her rise from AEDG Business Development Director
  to President/CEO by August 2024.
- **Executive Director of the Port Authority of Allen County (PAAC)** — she signs the
  PAAC records policy in that capacity, and recurs throughout the board minutes
  reporting on the deal (e.g. 2026-03-30, tying the N. Cole Street roadway
  improvements to "the Google data center project").

## Why the dual role matters

PAAC has **no employees** of its own; it must be administered by an external entity
([records policy](../extracted/aedg/paac-records-policy.policy.yaml)). With Leis serving as
**both** AEDG President/CEO and PAAC Executive Director, the same individual sits on
both sides of the front-end developer-information shield (R.C. 4582.58 — developer
information routed *through AEDG* is treated as a non-record until the employer commits
in writing) **and** the records custody for the public authority that approves the
deal. That single locus of control over the econ-dev shield + records is the core of
the records-completeness concern. See the memory note `leis-aedg-paac-dual-role`.

In the board minutes she describes roundabout phasing to objecting residents
(2025-08-07), and the PAAC board invokes the R.C. 4582.58(B) trade-secret shield to
enter executive session (2026-03-30) — the shield in active use.

## Research status

Roles and the dual capacity are read directly from the cited extractions and are
**common-control plumbing and leads to verify — not** statements about beneficial
ownership or wrongdoing. To extend: confirm the exact AEDG/PAAC contractual
administration arrangement and the dates of each appointment from primary records.

name: Jill Tangeman
summary: Vorys counsel for Bistrozzi LLC — company counsel on the Roadwork Development Agreement, the land-option assignments, and a recurring contact of record across the EPA permit file.
body:
## How she appears in the record

Jill S. Tangeman is **Vorys, Sater, Seymour and Pease** counsel on the company
(Bistrozzi/BOSC) side, recurring across three threads:

- **Company counsel on the Roadwork Development Agreement** — named in the RDA notice
  block as company counsel (`jstangeman@vorys.com`)
  ([RDA](../extracted/aedg/roadwork-development-agreement.rda.yaml)).
- **The land-option assignments** — the PAAC purchase options (Brenneman, Neff, Pike
  Run/Miller) were **assigned to Bistrozzi LLC** through Vorys/Tangeman (2025-07-03),
  closing 2025-07-14 ([seller-land-packets](../extracted/aedg/seller-land-packets.land.yaml)).
- **Permit contact of record** — she appears as `permit_contact` on numerous EPA
  permit extractions (entity graph: permit_contact ×11).

She also appears (with Leis and Rex Huffman) in the Neff property **Conditional Use
Permit** process in the PAAC board minutes (2024-10-24).

## Why this matters

Tangeman and Scott Ziance are the two Vorys hands on the local deal paperwork: Ziance
on the CRA/NDA/SOS filings, Tangeman on the RDA and the land-option assignment chain.
Together they are the developer-side legal channel through which the land assembly and
the road/CRA instruments were executed.

## Research status

Roles are read from the cited extractions and are **common-control plumbing and leads
to verify — not** statements about beneficial ownership or wrongdoing. To extend:
confirm the assignment instruments' recording details and her signature blocks.

name: John R. Willamowski, Jr.
summary: Assistant Prosecuting Attorney for Allen County; County counsel of record on the Roadwork Development Agreement and the originator of the County–Bistrozzi Mutual NDA.
body:
## How he appears in the record

John R. Willamowski, Jr. is an **Assistant Prosecuting Attorney for Allen County** —
i.e. the County's own counsel — and he appears at two load-bearing points:

- **Originator of the County–Bistrozzi Mutual NDA.** The NDA recitals state that
  "correspondence has been received from Assistant Prosecutor John Willamowski Jr.,
  requesting the Board enter into a Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement with Bistrozzi,
  LLC." The County's own counsel originated the instrument whose §6 became the
  contractual records-withholding engine (≥10 business days' notice to Bistrozzi
  before answering any PRR; disclose only the legal minimum; seek confidential
  treatment).
- **County counsel of record on the Roadwork Development Agreement** (and a notice
  copy recipient), per the RDA notice block.

## Why this matters

The NDA he originated is one of three stacked records-withholding mechanisms in the
deal (NDA §6 / CRA §22 / RDA §9.13), layered on top of the front-end R.C. 4582.58
econ-dev shield. That the *County's own counsel* requested the Board bind itself to
advance-notice-to-the-developer before answering public-records requests is central
to the mandamus narrative.

## Research status

Read from the cited extractions. The "originator" characterization is quoted from
the NDA's own recitals (document); his broader role in the County's records posture
is a **lead to verify** against primary correspondence, not an accusation.

**Identity — do not conflate with his father.** This is John R. Willamowski **Jr.**,
the Assistant County Prosecutor. His father, **John R. Willamowski Sr.**, is a
separate, still-active figure in the Ohio judiciary (the "Jr." in the slug and name is
load-bearing). Confirm which Willamowski is named on any instrument before relying on
identity in a filing.

name: Scott J. Ziance
summary: Organizer and contact of record on the Project BOSC entities and approvals.
body:
## How he appears in the record

Scott J. Ziance recurs across the Project BOSC corpus in two roles:

- **Organizer** of **Bistrozzi Addition LLC**. The Secretary of State filing names
  the organizer as *Scott J. Ziance* and records that the filing was *submitted via
  Vorys, Sater, Seymour and Pease LLP* (52 East Gay Street, Columbus), with C T
  Corporation as statutory agent.
- **Contact of record** on Ohio EPA / wetland-mitigation correspondence for the
  Project BOSC site (applicant **Bistrozzi LLC**), addressed to *Mr. Scott Ziance*
  at **52 East Gay Street, Columbus, OH 43215** — the Vorys office address.

The shared 52 East Gay Street address ties the permit contact and the Vorys filing
channel together in the record.

He also appears on the **deal instruments themselves**: as **company counsel for
Bistrozzi LLC** on the [CRA agreement](../extracted/legal/prr-mandamus/cra-agreement.cra.yaml)
(`sjziance@vorys.com`), and as the **authorized signatory who executed the Mutual NDA
for Bistrozzi** opposite the County's Brian Winegardner
([NDA](../extracted/legal/prr-mandamus/mutual-nda-bistrozzi.nda.yaml); Ziance signed
2025-07-01). Vorys handles the local CRA/land/NDA paperwork; cf. Jill Tangeman on the
RDA and the land-option assignments.

## Research status

Seeded from the entity graph (role: organizer ×1, permit_contact ×3) and verified
against the cited extractions below. The statements above are limited to what the
record shows; deeper biography (firm role, other engagements) is **not yet
researched** — extend this section as it is, with citations.

> Roles read from public records are *common-control plumbing* and leads to verify
> — **not** statements about beneficial ownership or wrongdoing.
